summary: LA County Forestry lookout on Oat Mountain, built 1923; cab now stands atop a telephone relay tower with a weather radar dome. Fire lookout use ended 1973.

facts.design: 1923: 30-foot X-brace steel tower with 8x8 observation cab (register; Angeles guide says 36 ft). 1937: replacement steel tower. 1951: lookout room atop a Pacific Telephone microwave relay tower
facts.status_note: Not a fire lookout since 1973. The cab stands on a telephone relay (antenna) tower and carries a weather radar dome; the register gives no removal date

staffing.status: manned by county lookouts; round-the-clock in WWII; closed as a lookout

access.note: Summit is inside Michael D. Antonovich Regional Park and reached by a paved road, but it is an antenna and equipment site; no source describes public access to the cab

visit.trail_note: Common approach is Brown Canyon Road from the Chatsworth side; past the first Nike-site remains, a few more strenuous miles lead to the summit

facts.agency: Los Angeles County Fire Department (register); built by the Los Angeles County Forestry Department in 1923

events.note: County Forestry Department lookout completed 1923; register gives a 30-ft X-brace steel tower with 8x8 cab, Angeles guide gives 36 ft

corrections.why: The fire lookout ended in 1973, but the cab still stands on a telephone relay tower and carries a KABC weather radar dome. Angeles Adventures lists the structure as 'Standing, re-purposed to an antenna tower'; the register's photo caption shows the radar atop the cab structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the 1923 tower as 30 feet and the Angeles guide as 36 feet. For the 1937 replacement, the county annual report says thirty feet and the Angeles guide says ten feet taller. Not resolved; the story gives the register figure and notes the guide's figure.

The register lists removal as unknown, the Angeles guide says the lookout closed in 1973 and the structure still stands, and the register says it was in use through at least 1968. These are consistent: the lookout closed later, the cab was kept as part of the relay tower.

A 1923 newspaper transcription calls the hill 'Oak Hill', near Newhall. The Forest Lookouts page files it under Oat Mountain, and the register and the guide give the same site. Whether 'Oak Hill' is a misprint or an older local name is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Status correction is the main finding: the record says gone, but the cab stands on a relay tower with a weather radar dome (Angeles Adventures and register photo caption; not seen first-hand). Height and replacement dimensions conflict across sources (30 vs 36 ft; 30 ft vs ten feet taller). The 1973 closure date comes from the Angeles guide alone; the register says in use through at least 1968. Staff names are from the Angeles guide and the 1924 newspaper quote; the guide's names are not checked against the Los Angeles Times or The Signal. The 1923 'Oak Hill' name needs a look. Access level is restricted because the summit is an equipment site; no source describes public access to the cab. Photos on the register page (1926 Los Angeles Times, 1963 The Signal) are credited but no image URLs were verified, so none were added. Two web searches and about six reads were used.
